review_notes: Re-review of the finite readiness-publication profile on 2026-10-03 by Claude (Claude Code) at the owner's direction after Codex was stopped. Controls are byte-identical to the 30 GiB capacity plan; that plan and the original 12 GiB plan are preserved unchanged.

Root cause of the prior SecureEmpty failures: the private-ACL helper ran inside Codex's unelevated Windows sandbox, whose restricted token lacks WRITE_DAC on the workspace (phase 8, HRESULT 0x80070005). The same helper passed all eight native fixture checks from an unsandboxed shell. Launch only from an unsandboxed process.

Changed since the capacity plan and reviewed: reference-private-acl.ps1 (DACL-only write, owner/inheritance/reparse/two-rule checks retained), private_acl_diagnostics.py and enterprise_reference_verify.py (closed numeric failure channel; ProgramData/SystemDrive environment fix), enterprise_wazuh_live_verify.py (fixed phase labels only), execution_policy.py (helper added to the frozen inventory; this plan registered). No control was loosened.
Use the already running local Linux engine and cached pinned image only. No Desktop starts/stops, downloads, networks, ports, other-project mounts, deletions or paid services.

The owner stopped the sibling AccessOps containers before this review; the preserved-workload limit remains eight and any baseline drift aborts the run. Cleanup targets only the exact owned collector.

Run f23cf0d7 (this plan's first revision) collected all 24 records and 8 alerts natively, then failed reconciliation: Wazuh derives record ids from the epoch second and alerts-file offset, so distinct events share ids. Reconciliation now treats a conflict as one id with different content for the same logical record; regression tests added.

Runs 4c03d55b (stopped at the launch memory guard) and 49d50e2a (24/8 collected; masked failure) followed. The in-image collector runs on Wazuh's bundled Python 3.10, which cannot parse Wazuh's own '+0000' timestamps. bridge.contract.timestamp now normalizes +HHMM to +HH:MM; verified under the image's Python 3.10 by replaying run 49d50e2a (24/24 archived, 8/8 alerted).

Recovery profile (--profile recovery) added under the same controls: half the records publish while the collector runs; after they are archived the driver stops wazuh-logcollector, the host rotates the largest input logrotate-style (rename aside, recreate at the same path) and writes the backlog, then the collector restarts. Acceptance additionally requires zero extra archive or alert copies.

Main and independent shutdown, exact source/native record/alert reconciliation and unchanged sampled preserved envelopes are all required. Snapshot compatibility and continuous delivery remain separate claims.
